He is covetous. He covets that which belongs to another, the wealth and property of others, thinking: 'Oh, that what belongs to another were mine!' He is malevolent in mind, possessed of corrupt intentions, thinking: 'May these beings be killed, or slaughtered, or destroyed, or perished, or may they cease to exist.' He has wrong view and a distorted perspective: 'There is no gift, there is no offering, there is no sacrifice. There is no fruit or result of good and bad deeds. There is no this world, no other world. There is no mother, no father. There is no spontaneously born being. There are no contemplatives and brahmins in the world who have reached the right path and are practicing rightly, who, having directly known and realized for themselves this world and the other world, make them known.'

Monks, one endowed with these ten qualities is cast into hell according to his deeds.

3. Monks, one endowed with ten qualities is cast into heaven according to his deeds. With which ten?

4. Here, monks, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from taking life. With the rod laid aside and the sword laid aside, he is conscientious, kind, and dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings. Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. Whatever is the wealth and property of another, whether in the village or the forest, he does not take it by way of theft. Having abandoned sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct. He does not have sexual relations with those protected by their mother, protected by their father, protected by their brother, protected by their sister, protected by their relatives, protected by their lineage <note>original: "dhammarakkhitā"; likely refers to legal or traditional protection</note>, those who have a husband, those under the threat of punishment, or even those garlanded with flowers <note>referring to those betrothed or engaged</note>. Having abandoned false speech, he abstains from false speech. When he goes to an assembly, a gathering, among his relatives, among a guild, or into the royal court, and is called as a witness and asked: 'Now, good man, tell what you know,' if he does not know, he says: 'I do not know'; if he knows, he says: 'I know'; if he has not seen, he says: 'I have not seen'; if he has seen, he says: 'I have seen.' Thus, neither for his own sake, nor for the sake of another, nor for the sake of some small material gain, does he speak a deliberate lie.

<summary>This page lists the ethical failures leading to rebirth in hell, specifically covetousness, ill-will, and wrong view. It then begins the description of the ten virtuous qualities leading to heaven, detailing the first four: non-violence, honesty, sexual propriety, and truthfulness.</summary>
